title: ALMA observations of the Extended Green Object G19.01-0.03 - I. A Keplerian disc in a massive protostellar system
question: What are the kinematic properties, centimetre-millimetre SED, disc stability, and nature of the central source(s) in the massive protostellar system G19.01–0.03 MM1?

data.sensitivity: 0.25 mJy beam^-1 (continuum); 3.0 mJy beam^-1 (wideband spectral line median); 7.2 mJy beam^-1 (narrow spw CH3OH line)

what.value: SMA 1.3 mm (275 +/- 7 mJy) and CARMA 3.4 mm (27 +/- 3 mJy) continuum flux densities for SED modelling, and SMA 12CO(2-1) outflow data

evidence.quote: The SED, presented in Figure [4](#fig:sed), includes our new VLA 1.21 cm and 5.01 cm and ALMA 1.05 mm data along with the SMA 1.3 mm and CARMA 3.4 mm datapoints from (cite: cyganowski11a).

what.value: NH3 LSRK velocity and Galactic rotation curve parameters used to estimate the near kinematic distance of 4.0 +/- 0.3 kpc

evidence.quote: Throughout, we adopt a near kinematic distance of $4.0\pm0.3$ kpc, estimated from the NH$_{3}$ LSRK velocity from (cite: cyganowski13) and the Galactic rotation curve parameters from (cite: reid14).

what.value: Dust temperature range of T_dust = 100-130 K and bolometric luminosity ~10^4 L_sun

evidence.quote: On this sizescale, for temperatures $T_{\mathrm{dust}}=100-130$ K (cite: cyganowski11a), we calculate dust optical depths $\tau_{\mathrm {dust}}$ $\sim$ $0.09-0.12$ and a gas mass M$_{\mathrm{gas}}$ $\sim$ $5.4-7.2$ M$_{\odot}$ for MM1.
The bolometric luminosity of G19.01–0.03 MM1 is $\sim$10$^{4}$ L$_{\odot}$ (cite: cyganowski11a).

what.value: JPL and CDMS molecular spectroscopic catalogues

evidence.loc: Compact molecular line emission towards MM1
evidence.quote: We use the JPL (cite: jpl) and CDMS (cite: cdms) catalogues to identify the observed molecular lines.

recipe.goal: Extract continuum source structures and properties
recipe.method: Dendrogram extraction on the ALMA 1.05 mm continuum image out to the 30% primary beam response level, and 2D Gaussian fitting on ALMA and VLA continuum images
key_parameters: I_min = 5 sigma_rms = 1.25 mJy beam^-1, Delta I_min = 1 sigma_rms = 0.25 mJy beam^-1, n_pix = 25 pixels

recipe.goal: Identify molecular line transitions and map velocity gradients
recipe.method: Cross-match observed lines with JPL and CDMS catalogues, generate LTE synthetic spectra with CLASS/Weeds to confirm detections, compute moment 1 maps, and measure velocity gradient position angles from the slope connecting most blue-shifted and red-shifted positions
key_parameters: 19 lines in broad spws + 1 narrow-band CH3OH line; 3 lines with extended emission excluded from disc PA and inclination averages
assumptions: LTE conditions with hot core rotational temperatures > 100 K

recipe.goal: Fit 6.7 GHz Class II CH3OH maser positions and ring geometry
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussian point sources to each channel with >5 sigma maser detection using CASA IMFIT, then fit an ellipse to the maser positions
key_parameters: >5 sigma detection criterion per channel; point source fit with axes and PA fixed to synthesised beam
assumptions: Maser emission is unresolved in each channel; circular symmetry assumed when estimating inclination of the maser ring

recipe.goal: Estimate disc inclination angle and model position-velocity (PV) diagrams
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussians to moment 0 maps of 17 compact lines and 1.05 mm continuum to derive inclination i assuming circular symmetry; compare theoretical PV models of a thin Keplerian disc + freefall infall against observed PV diagrams sliced perpendicular to the outflow
key_parameters: i = 40 deg, R_out = 2000 AU (or 3500 AU for extended lines), R_in = 1700 AU (fixed to beamsize)
assumptions: Thin circumstellar disc with circular symmetry in Keplerian rotation and freefall infall; d = 4.0 kpc

recipe.method: Re-image VLA 1.21 cm with uv-range > 20 klambda and split VLA 5.01 cm into two halves (6.00 cm and 4.30 cm); measure fluxes with 2D Gaussian fits; fit a two-component model (single-temperature modified greybody dust + uniform sphere Bremsstrahlung HC HII region) to 6 datapoints
key_parameters: 7 model parameters: n_e, R_e, T_e, theta_d, T_d, beta, tau_1.3mm; 6 independent flux datapoints (6.00 cm, 4.30 cm, 1.21 cm, 3.4 mm, 1.3 mm, 1.05 mm)
assumptions: Uniform sphere geometry for HC HII region; single-temperature modified greybody for dust; flux calibration uncertainties of 5% (VLA), 10% (ALMA), 15% (SMA, CARMA)

recipe.goal: Derive disc gas mass and evaluate gravitational stability
recipe.method: Calculate isothermal dust-derived gas mass with optical depth correction from the 1.05 mm integrated flux density, then compute the disc-to-star mass ratio M_d / M_*
assumptions: Isothermal dust emission, d = 4.0 kpc, gas-to-dust mass ratio R = 100, kappa_1.05mm = 1.45 cm^2 g^-1, stability threshold M_d / M_* = 0.1

answer_key.quantity: MM1 ALMA 1.05 mm continuum peak intensity (astrodendro)
MM1 ALMA 1.05 mm continuum integrated flux (astrodendro)
MM1 ALMA 1.05 mm continuum deconvolved size (astrodendro)
MM1 ALMA 1.05 mm continuum integrated flux (2D Gaussian fit)
CM1 VLA 1.21 cm peak intensity
CM1 VLA 1.21 cm integrated flux
CM1 VLA 5.01 cm peak intensity
CM1 VLA 5.01 cm integrated flux
Positional offset of VLA 5.01 cm emission from ALMA 1.05 mm peak

evidence.quote: Interestingly, the 5.01 cm emission is offset to the southwest by $\sim$0.16$''$ ($\sim$640 AU), $\sim$2.4$\times$ the absolute positional uncertainty of the 5.01 cm data (estimated as 10 per cent of the geometric mean of the synthesised beam).

answer_key.quantity: Mean position angle of molecular line velocity gradient

evidence.loc: Compact molecular line emission towards MM1
evidence.quote: For the 16 lines in Figure [3](#fig:mom1) shown to have compact emission (excluding the 3 with more extended emission) and the narrow-band CH$_{3}$OH line in Figure [4](#fig:masers)a, we find a mean position angle of $78.0 \pm 8.0 ^{\circ}$ (with standard error), in agreement with the position angle of MM1 from the 1.05 mm continuum of $78.7^{\circ}$.

answer_key.quantity: Angle between candidate disc PA and bipolar outflow PA

evidence.loc: Compact molecular line emission towards MM1
evidence.quote: The position angle of the candidate disc is $96.5\pm9.4^{\circ}$ from that of the outflow, consistent with a perpendicular orientation and the observation of a disc-outflow system.

answer_key.quantity: 6.7 GHz CH3OH maser ring fitted ellipse size

evidence.quote: An ellipse fitted to the maser positions (excluding the outlier with large uncertainties in Figure [4](#fig:masers)b) has a size of $0.151\ensuremath{''}\times0.072\ensuremath{''}\sim 600 \times 290$ AU (major $\times$ minor axis) and a position angle of $\sim80^{\circ}$.

answer_key.quantity: Disc inclination angle from 17 molecular lines (median)

evidence.quote: The inclination angles calculated for these 17 lines range from $i=19-64^{\circ}$, with a median of $i=38^{\circ}$ and a standard deviation of 10$^{\circ}$.

answer_key.quantity: Disc inclination angle from 1.05 mm dust continuum

evidence.quote: The equivalent calculation for $i$ using the deconvolved 1.05 mm source size from Table [\[tab:leaves\]](#tab:leaves) yields $i=43^{\circ}$ for the dust emission, in reasonable agreement with the median value of 38$^{\circ}$ from the lines.

answer_key.quantity: Enclosed mass M_enc (within R_out = 2000 AU for i = 40 deg)

evidence.quote: Kinematic modelling shows the data are well described by models that include a disc in Keplerian rotation and infall, with an enclosed mass of $40-70$ M$_{\odot}$ (within a 2000 AU outer radius) for a disc inclination angle of $i=40^{\circ}$, of which $5.4-7.2$ M$_{\odot}$ is attributed to the disc.

answer_key.quantity: Centimetre-wavelength spectral index (6.00 cm to 4.30 cm)

evidence.quote: The centimetre-wavelength spectral index calculated from these datapoints, $\alpha_{\rm 6.00cm-4.30cm}=1.5\pm1.1$ (S$_{\nu}$ $\propto$ $\nu^{\alpha}$), is consistent with moderately optically thick free-free emission from a hypercompact (HC) H ii region or ionised jet (cite: moscadelli16; purser16; yang19).

answer_key.quantity: Best-fit HC HII region radius R_e

evidence.quote: The best-fitting model, shown in Figure [4](#fig:sed), has an H ii region radius R$_e$=33 AU (cite: cyganowski11b), an electron temperature of 9700 K, and an electron density of 8.6$\times$10$^{5}$ cm$^{-3}$; the dust component is optically thick at millimetre wavelengths ($\tau_{\mathrm{1.3mm}}$=7), with a diameter of 1140 AU, $\beta$=2.0, and T$_d$=69 K.

answer_key.quantity: Best-fit dust emissivity index beta

evidence.quote: The best-fitting model, shown in Figure [4](#fig:sed), has an H ii region radius R$_e$=33 AU (cite: cyganowski11b), an electron temperature of 9700 K, and an electron density of 8.6$\times$10$^{5}$ cm$^{-3}$; the dust component is optically thick at millimetre wavelengths ($\tau_{\mathrm{1.3mm}}$=7), with a diameter of 1140 AU, $\beta$=2.0, and T$_d$=69 K.

answer_key.quantity: Disc gas mass M_gas (for T_dust = 100-130 K)

evidence.quote: On this sizescale, for temperatures $T_{\mathrm{dust}}=100-130$ K (cite: cyganowski11a), we calculate dust optical depths $\tau_{\mathrm {dust}}$ $\sim$ $0.09-0.12$ and a gas mass M$_{\mathrm{gas}}$ $\sim$ $5.4-7.2$ M$_{\odot}$ for MM1.

answer_key.quantity: Central stellar mass M_* (M_enc - M_d)

evidence.quote: For MM1, attributing the $M_{\mathrm{gas}}$ estimated above to the disc and estimating the stellar mass as $M_{\ast}=M_{\mathrm{enc}}-M_{d}\simeq33-65$ M$_{\odot}$, we find $M_{d}/M_{\ast}\sim0.08-0.22$.

answer_key.quantity: Disc-to-star mass ratio M_d / M_*

evidence.quote: For MM1, attributing the $M_{\mathrm{gas}}$ estimated above to the disc and estimating the stellar mass as $M_{\ast}=M_{\mathrm{enc}}-M_{d}\simeq33-65$ M$_{\odot}$, we find $M_{d}/M_{\ast}\sim0.08-0.22$.

not_stated_but_needed: Exact frequency/channel ranges flagged as line-free to construct the ~1.6 GHz ALMA pseudo-continuum dataset
Self-calibration solution intervals, number of iterations, and whether amplitude self-calibration was performed in addition to phase self-calibration for ALMA continuum
Imaging cell size, image pixel dimensions, and cleaning stopping thresholds / masking strategy for ALMA continuum and spectral line cubes
Whether continuum subtraction in the uv-plane (e.g. uvcontsub) was applied to the ALMA spectral line cubes before imaging
Exact LTE synthetic spectrum parameters (column densities, excitation temperatures, linewidths, source size) used in CLASS/Weeds for line identification
Velocity ranges and intensity thresholds used when computing moment 0 and moment 1 maps for the 20 molecular lines
Exact slice width and central coordinates used to extract the position-velocity (PV) diagrams
missing_for_reproduction: Exact channel/frequency masks used to define the ~1.6 GHz line-free continuum bandwidth
Self-calibration solution intervals, number of rounds, and clean masking details for ALMA and VLA
Custom scripts used for the analytical PV curve generation and the two-stage 7-parameter SED grid fitting
score_reason: Observing setups, calibration pipeline versions, robust weighting parameters, astrodendro parameters, rest frequencies, and analytical equations for PV and dust mass are all clearly stated. However, self-calibration parameters, line-free channel masks, and custom PV/SED fitting scripts are not released, and PV fitting is done by eye.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA data (2013.1.00812.S) and VLA data (13B-359) with well-defined numeric targets (continuum fluxes, source sizes via astrodendro and IMFIT, line velocity gradient PAs, isothermal gas mass, and enclosed mass constraints).
